conviction_note: The findings sum to +0.6. Ouster has beaten the midpoint of its own revenue guide by 4.5% and 7.1% in the last two quarters, and robotics peers printed strong, but this name sold a 7% beat last quarter (-4.8%) on a soft next-quarter guide, the Q4 guide is unknown against an implied ~$61m consensus, and the 25-delta skew is +17 vol points toward downside. So p_up sits at 51 against an abs move of 14 (the option-implied move is 16.0%, the name's median reaction 6.9%), giving +0.28. The scaled number is smaller than the sum because the guide decides this print and my evidence on the guide is inference.

FY2026 revenue consensus is $221.5m from 6 analysts (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/oust/forecast/, checked 2026-10-22), which implies Q4 at about $61m if Q3 lands near $57m. My print estimate is ~$58.5m, about +2.5% over a ~$57m bar.

findings.finding: Ouster has beaten the midpoint of its own revenue guide in each of the last two quarters. Q1 2026 came in at $48.6m against a $45-48m guide (+4.5% vs midpoint) and Q2 2026 at $54.6m against $49.5-52.5m (+7.1% vs midpoint). The same pattern on the Q3 guide of $54.5-57.5m (midpoint $56.0m) implies roughly $58.5-60m, against a sell-side bar of about $57.5m. Management did say on the Q2 call that upside to the guide is limited unless the Rev8 production ramp, due late in Q3, can be accelerated.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat consensus by about 6-7% ($54.6m vs ~$51.5m) and the stock fell 4.78% on a soft Q3 guide. Q1 2026 beat its guide and the stock rose 2.78%. This name sells top-line beats when the guide disappoints.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $57.5-57.7m already sits above the guide midpoint, so a beat of about $1-2m is partly expected. If the market expected the full historical beat, consensus would sit near $59-60m. The 'limited upside' comment from the call is the reason it does not.
findings.independence: Q1 guide versus actual comes from a different document, the Q1 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001816581/000119312526206501/d947395dex991.htm). The 'limited upside' caveat is from the call summary (https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/ouster-inc-earnings-call-highlights-growth-momentum), which argues against the size and was netted into it.

findings.finding: The print turns on the Q4 guide. FY2026 consensus of $221.5m (6 analysts) less H1 actuals of $103.2m and a ~$57m Q3 implies the street holds Q4 at about $61m. In both of the last two quarters Ouster guided the next quarter with a midpoint at or below consensus: the Q3 guide midpoint of $56.0m sat against $57.7m consensus, and the stock fell 4.8%. A Q4 midpoint of about $60m would repeat that. Q4 2025 total revenue of $62.2m also included $21.2m of mostly one-time royalties, so total revenue in Q4 2026 will look roughly flat year on year even though product revenue grows about 45%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-06): Q3 guide midpoint below consensus, stock -4.78% despite a beat. Q3 2025 (2025-11-04): -6.54%. Q4 2025 (2026-03-02), where the long-term 30-50% growth framework was reiterated: +7.26%.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q4 bar is implied by full-year totals and nobody publishes it; previews quote only the Q3 range. If the market expected a below-consensus Q4 guide, the FY2026 consensus would already have been cut toward ~$218m, and the analyst range ($219-225m) shows it has not. The -33% run-up and the downside skew may already hold part of this.
findings.independence: The Q4 2025 royalty figure comes from the Q4 2025 release (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260302613164/en/Ouster-Announces-Results-for-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025). The guide-versus-consensus pattern comes from MarketBeat's 2026-08-07 coverage cited in the bar. This is an inference from a pattern, not a company document about Q4.

findings.finding: Q2 2026 GAAP gross margin of 49% (non-GAAP 53%) included a one-time $5.4m cost reduction from IEEPA import-duty refunds, about 1,000bp, which management said will not recur. The full $4.8m receivable was collected after quarter end, and the 10-Q names no further refunds. Q3 gross margin therefore steps down sequentially, toward the low-to-mid 40s non-GAAP. Industry memory-price inflation may also hit hardware margins: Cognex guided a 75bp Q3 hit from memory prices, and DRAM contract prices roughly doubled in Q1 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin has not been the reaction line in the baseline history; the moves followed revenue guidance. Q4 2025 printed a royalty-inflated 60% GAAP margin with the stock +7.26%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: management flagged the refund as one-time on the call, so the step-down sits inside what the company told the market. The part that may not be priced is memory-cost pressure. If consensus held Q3 margin at 53%, the non-GAAP EPS bar would sit near breakeven rather than -$0.08 to -$0.14.
findings.independence: The memory proxy comes from Cognex's Q2 call (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/cognex-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-06/) and TrendForce/Counterpoint pricing (https://carnewschina.com/2026/04/28/byd-price-hike-lidar-adas-hits-1660-usd-as-dram-costs-soar/). It is a proxy that Ouster has not confirmed.

findings.finding: Counterparties and peers that reported after Ouster last spoke show robotics and physical-AI hardware demand intact. Teradyne Robotics posted a record Q3 of $96m, up about 28% year on year and profitable (8-K, 2026-10-27). RoboSense's Q3 robotics lidar volume rose 309% year on year to 145,200 units (2026-10-09). Ouster's growth comes from industrial (warehouse automation) and smart infrastructure, per its Q2 release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior Ouster reaction tied to peer prints. In the sector sessions (2026-08-03 rally, 08-18 selloff) OUST moved with AEVA and SYM in the same direction.
findings.why_not_priced: OUST fell 33% over the same 20 days these peers reported healthy robotics demand. If the price held this demand read, the lidar names would not have fallen in step with AI semis on 10-30. RoboSense's growth is also a pricing-competition threat, which caps the size.
findings.independence: RoboSense Q3 volumes, a different source: https://autonews.gasgoo.com/articles/news/robosense-quarterly-lidar-sales-hit-new-high-in-q3-2026-2108495209121140737. Both are proxies; neither names Ouster.

findings.finding: Ouster's 20-day fall of 33% (from about $44 on 2026-10-05 to $30.08) has no company-specific cause in EDGAR: no 8-K and no offering since 08-06, and the only Form 4 is a director taking fees in stock at $44.12. It ran in step with peer AEVA (down 28.6% month to date by 10-16) and with the 10-30 AI/semis rout. Consensus price targets ($54-59) and estimates were not cut over that period, so the bar did not move while the price fell.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2024 and Q1 2025 prints after drawdowns rose +31.9% and +22.8% (2025-03-20, 2025-05-08). The 2025-11-04 print, which came after a run-up, fell 6.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is positioning, not a fact: the skew of +17 vol points says the market still pays for downside after the fall, against this finding. It is sized near zero because a sector-driven drawdown is not evidence that the print will be read kindly.

findings.finding: Forterra announced on 2026-10-21 an expanded multi-year partnership to put Ouster REV8 native-color lidar in its AutoDrive autonomy platform, which runs on more than 50 vehicle platforms in more than 10 countries. A separate release that day said Ouster sensors run in Forterra's Lancer vehicles in Ukraine across more than 1,400 missions. Together they point to a defense revenue line that management may quantify on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print reaction is tied to defense commentary. The stock fell on the days around the release.
findings.why_not_priced: The release is public, but no dollar figure is attached. It would be priced if defense were quoted as a revenue line in previews, and it is not.
findings.independence: The partnership is also reported at https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260507729786/en/ (the May 2026 Ouster/Forterra context). This rests on one company release.

findings.finding: There is no financing overhang into the print. Ouster raised about $98m on an ATM that is now fully used and closed, plus $191.9m in a July 2026 underwritten offering. That gives pro forma liquidity of about $455m against an adjusted EBITDA loss of about $4.5m a quarter, with no debt. The raises fund Rev8 capacity at Benchmark (target over 100,000 units a year) and inventory, which rose from $23.6m to $31.4m with raw materials up from $3.9m to $11.1m. That is a ramp, and the ramp is corroborated.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prior raises (July 2026 offering, May ATM) drew -7% to -17% reactions on announcement days. No print day carried a raise.
findings.why_not_priced: After two dilutive raises in 2026 and a stock down 52% from its high, part of the market may fear another ATM filed with the 10-Q. If that fear were absent, the post-raise discount would have closed.
findings.independence: The share-sale size comes from a different source, IFR: https://www.ifre.com/equities/2437962/ouster-scales-up-growth-with-us200m-stock-sale. The cash and inventory figures come from the same 10-Q as the margin finding.

findings.finding: The Amazon warrant is nearly fully vested. At 2026-06-30, 3,161,365 of 3,290,094 warrant shares had vested, leaving about 129k. The fair value of each vesting is booked as a non-cash reduction to revenue; it cut H1 revenue by $2.375m. That drag is close to its end, a small tailwind to reported GAAP revenue. 'Customer E' was 32% of Q2 revenue and is probably Amazon, which makes concentration a two-way risk.
findings.why_not_priced: Too small to be modelled separately. The concentration figure sits in the 10-Q notes, not in previews.
findings.independence: Same 10-Q as the margin and financing findings. Customer E's identity as Amazon is my inference, not disclosed.

findings.finding: The CEO (30,385 shares) and the General Counsel (11,484 shares) sold at $33.96 on 2026-09-14, after six Form 144s were filed 2026-09-11. Insiders sold 173k shares ($6.7m) over the quarter. The pattern matches sell-to-cover on an RSU vest date, not a discretionary signal.
findings.why_not_priced: These are public Form 4s. They would matter only if discretionary, and the same-day multi-officer pattern says they are not.
findings.independence: EDGAR filing list (Form 144s on 09-11, Form 4s on 09-16): https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001816581&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40

findings.finding: Vanguard Capital Management filed a Schedule 13G on 2026-10-30 reporting 3,606,687 shares (5%) as of 2026-09-30, with sole voting power over only 536,479. This is passive ownership crossing the reporting threshold.
findings.why_not_priced: Index-driven holding; there is nothing for the print to reprice.

rejected_candidates.detail: Q1 2026 GAAP gross margin of 43% and Q2 ex-refund of about 39% GAAP / 43% non-GAAP (8-K and 10-Q) contradict a 35-40% product norm as a stated guide. The underlying refund fact is kept in the margin finding.

baseline_tension: My findings lean slightly positive (a guide-beat pattern, intact peer demand, no financing overhang). That cuts against the +17-point put skew and the -33% run-up, which the market reads as downside still to come; the Q4-guide risk is the one finding on the skew's side, so p_up stays at 51.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold a 7% beat at -4.8%): the guide-beat finding went from +1.0 to +0.7.
Lessons 5 and 7 (a drawdown with no cause in EDGAR is worth about 0; a sign against a strong skew needs a reason): the positioning/drawdown finding went from +0.5 to +0.2, and p_up from 52 to 51.

Lesson 6 and the core table (a finding inside what the company already guided goes toward 0): the margin step-down from the tariff refund went from -0.5 to -0.3, since management told the market it would not recur.

Lesson 2 (name the line): the Q4 guidance finding left standing at -1.0 as the line this name trades on. Lesson 4 (financing): the financing finding stays positive because inventory and capacity corroborate a ramp.
The core rule that understatement is systematic, plus the 16% implied move: abs_move_pct raised from 13 to 14.
